info.title: Co-Found Platform API
info.description:
Complete REST API for the Co-Found collaboration platform.

## Authentication
All protected endpoints require a Bearer token obtained from `/api/auth/login`.
Include it in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer {token}`

## Modules
- **Authentication** — Register, login, email verification, password reset, identity verification
- **Profile** — User profile, skills, endorsements, portfolio
- **Projects** — CRUD, roles, skills, milestones, team members
- **Applications** — Apply, review, manage project applications
- **Collaboration** — Connections, invitations, matches, ratings
- **Communication** — Conversations, messages, files, video calls, notifications
- **Administration** — Reports, moderation, restrictions, system settings (admin/moderator only)

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's current identity verification record.

Returns **404** if the user has not submitted a verification yet.

post.description:
Submits identity documents for review. Accepts `multipart/form-data`.

## Business rules
- **Max 3 attempts** per user. Returns 429 after limit is reached.
- **Resubmission**: only allowed if the previous status is `rejected`.
  Returns 409 for `pending`, `under_review`, `escalated`, and `verified`.
- **One account per ID card**: if the card number is already associated
  with a verified account, returns 409.
- Document images are stored **privately** — paths are never returned.
- `id_card_number` is stored **encrypted** — never returned to the client.

## After submission
Status is `pending`. A moderator will claim and review the submission.
Poll `GET /verification` to check for status changes.

## Liveness check data
Pass the raw JSON output from your frontend liveness SDK as a JSON string
in the `liveness_check_data` field. The backend stores it for the ML pipeline.

id_card_image_front.description: Front face of the identity document. Max 10MB. jpg/png/webp.

id_card_image_back.description: Back face of the identity document. Max 10MB. jpg/png/webp.

id_card_number.description: National ID or passport number. Stored encrypted. Used for duplicate detection.

full_name_on_card.description: Full name exactly as it appears on the document.

submission_method.description: How the document images were captured.

liveness_check_data.description: JSON string from frontend liveness SDK. Pass the raw SDK output as a string.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's match queue, sorted by score descending by default.

**Filters:**
- `match_type` — `collaborator` or `project`
- `viewed` — `true` or `false`
- `saved` — `true` or `false`
- `min_score` — e.g. `0.7` to see only high-confidence matches

**Sorting:**
- `sort_by` — `compatibility_score` | `created_at` | `expires_at`
- `sort_dir` — `asc` | `desc` (default: `desc`)

post.description:
Creates a new call, adds the initiator as host participant, and returns a short-lived Jitsi JWT (`join_token`) so the initiator can enter the room immediately — no second `/join` call needed.

**Context (exactly one required):**
- `conversation_id` — restricts join access to participants of that conversation (1-to-1 or group)
- `project_id` — restricts join access to active members of that project team

Both IDs together, or neither, are rejected with **422**.
`call_type` is derived automatically from whichever ID is provided — it is not sent by the client.

**Status:**
- `scheduled` (default) — activates when the first other participant joins
- `active` — starts immediately

**JWT usage:** build the Jitsi URL as `{room_url}?jwt={join_token}` and open it in an iframe or redirect. The token is scoped to the specific room and expires after 4 hours.

conversation_id.description: Link the call to a conversation. Exactly one of `conversation_id` or `project_id` must be provided.

project_id.description: Link the call to a project. Exactly one of `conversation_id` or `project_id` must be provided.

start_time.description: Must be in the future. Omit for an instant call.

201.description: Call created. The response includes `join_token` — a short-lived Jitsi JWT the initiator uses to enter the room immediately.

get.description:
Returns paginated calls the authenticated user initiated or participated in,
ordered by most recent first. Useful for displaying call history.

Returns full call detail.
`room_url` is `null` for non-participants — they must call `/join` first.
`join_token` is **never** returned by this endpoint; use `/join` to obtain one.

post.description:
Adds the authenticated user as a participant and returns a short-lived Jitsi JWT (`join_token`). The frontend builds the final Jitsi URL as `{room_url}?jwt={join_token}`.

**Access control:**
- Project call → must be an active project team member (or the initiator)
- Conversation call → must be an active conversation participant (or the initiator)
Every call must have a context — ad-hoc access is not supported.

**Rejoin:** If you previously left, your existing participant row is updated (`left_at` cleared) — not duplicated. A fresh JWT is issued.

**Idempotent:** Calling join when already active in the call is safe — returns 200 with a fresh JWT. Useful for reconnecting after a page refresh or network drop.

**Auto-activates:** Joining a `scheduled` call changes its status to `active`.

**Returns 409** if the call is `ended` or `cancelled`.
**Returns 409** if you are not a member of the linked project or conversation.

200.description: Joined successfully. `join_token` is a short-lived Jitsi JWT scoped to this room. Build the Jitsi URL as `{room_url}?jwt={join_token}` and open it in an iframe or redirect.

401.description: Call is not joinable (already ended or cancelled)

post.description:
Records the user's departure and calculates their `duration_seconds`.
If no active participants remain after leaving, the call automatically
ends and `status` becomes `ended`.
**Returns 403** if you are not an active participant.
**Returns 409** if the call has already ended or been cancelled.

patch.description:
Forcefully ends an **active** call. Host only.
All participants are marked as left and duration is recorded.

**Only works on active calls.** For scheduled calls that haven't started,
use `PATCH /calls/{id}/cancel` instead — this returns 409 on scheduled calls.

**Returns 403** if you are not the call initiator.
**Returns 409** if the call is already ended, cancelled, or still scheduled.

Cancels a **scheduled** call before it starts. Host (initiator) only.
No participants are affected since the call never went active.

**Only works on scheduled calls.** For active calls, use `PATCH /calls/{id}/end`.
**Returns 403** if you are not the call initiator.
**Returns 409** if the call is already active, ended, or cancelled.

patch.description:
Marks the verification as `under_review` so only one moderator works
a case at a time.

**Claimable states:** `pending`, `escalated`

**Transitions:**
- `pending` → `under_review`
- `escalated` → `under_review`

**Returns 409** if the verification is already `under_review`, `verified`, or `rejected`.

Logs a `verification_claimed` entry to `admin_actions`.

patch.description:
Escalates a verification that is currently `under_review` to the `escalated`
status for administrator attention.

**Escalatable state:** `under_review` only

**Returns 409** if the verification is not `under_review`.

Logs a `verification_escalated` entry to `admin_actions`.

post.description:
Creates a `regular_user` account with `account_status=pending`.

**What happens on success:**
- User row created with `email_verified=false`, `account_status=pending`
- Verification email dispatched (token valid 24 h)
- Sanctum token returned immediately — client can call `/auth/me` and
  `/auth/email/resend` without re-logging in
- Write routes remain blocked by the `verified` middleware until the
  email is confirmed

**Password rules:** min 8 chars, at least one uppercase letter,
one lowercase letter, and one digit.

**Username rules:** 3–30 chars, letters / digits / underscores only.

201.description: Registered — verification email sent, token returned

message.example: Registration successful. Please check your email to verify your account.

example.message: Registration successful. Please check your email to verify your account.

post.description:
Creates an ephemeral `role=guest` user row and issues a 7-day Sanctum token.

**What guests can do:** browse public projects and user listings.

**What guests cannot do:** any write or social action — create projects,
apply, connect, send invitations, rate collaborators, message, etc.
All blocked actions return `403 GUEST_ACCESS_RESTRICTED`.

**Upgrading:** when a guest registers, a new `regular_user` account is
created. The guest row is cleaned up by the daily `auth:prune-guests` command.

**Rate limit:** 5 requests per minute per IP.

example.message: Guest session started. Create an account to unlock all features.

post.description:
Authenticates with email + password and returns a Sanctum token.

**Guard order (security-relevant):**
1. User must exist
2. Brute-force lock check — checked before password to avoid timing hints
3. Password verification — failure increments attempt counter
4. Account status — `banned`, `suspended`, `deleted` → `403`
5. Active `full_suspension` restriction → `403`
6. Issue token, reset counter, record `last_login_at`

**Pending users** (`account_status=pending`, email not verified) **can log in.**
They receive a token but write routes are soft-blocked.

**Brute-force lock:** 5 consecutive failures → 15-minute account lock → `423`
with `locked_until` timestamp. Correct credentials during lock still return `423`.

**All previous tokens are revoked** on successful login (single active session).

423.description: Account locked — too many failed attempts

example.message: Account is temporarily locked due to too many failed login attempts.

get.description:
Consumes the one-time token sent to the user's inbox.

**On success:**
- `email_verified` → `true`
- `account_status` → `active`
- Token columns cleared

Token is valid for **24 hours**.
Use `/auth/email/resend` to get a new one if it expires.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: 64-character random string from the verification email

200.description: Email verified — account is now active

example.message: Email verified successfully. Your account is now active.
The verification token is invalid or has expired.
Email address has already been verified.

post.description:
Sends a reset link to the email if an account exists.

**Always returns `200`** regardless of whether the email is registered —
prevents user enumeration attacks.

Each call invalidates all previous reset tokens for that user.
Only one valid token exists per user at any time.
Token is valid for **60 minutes**.

**Rate limit:** 5 requests per minute per IP.

200.description: Response is identical whether or not the email exists

example.message: If an account exists with that email, a reset link has been sent.

post.description:
Validates the reset token and updates the password.

**On success:**
- Password updated
- Reset token marked as `used` (preserved for audit)
- All other reset tokens for the user deleted
- **All Sanctum tokens revoked** — forces re-login on every device

A used token cannot be replayed — subsequent calls with the same token
return `400`.

**Password rules:** min 8 chars, at least one uppercase letter,
one lowercase letter, and one digit.

**Rate limit:** 5 requests per minute per IP.

200.description: Password reset — login with new credentials

example.message: Password reset successfully. Please log in with your new password.

400.description: Token invalid, expired, or already used

example.message: The password reset token is invalid or has expired.

post.description:

post.description:
Revokes the current token and issues a fresh one.
Use to extend sessions without re-entering credentials.
Works for both guest and regular user tokens.

Generates a fresh 24-hour token and resends the verification email.
Each call **invalidates** the previous token — old verification links

**Requires:** a real user token (`no.guest` enforced).
**Returns `409`** if the email is already verified.
**Rate limit:** 3 requests per minute per IP.

403.description: Guest tokens cannot access this endpoint

patch.description:
Records that the user has viewed this match. Sets `viewed=true` and `viewed_at`.
**Idempotent** — safe to call multiple times, only sets the timestamp on first call.

patch.summary: Toggle save state of a match
patch.description:
Toggles the `saved` field. If the match is currently unsaved it becomes saved, and vice versa.
Returns `"Match saved."` or `"Match unsaved."` in the message field.

post.description:
Records the user's explicit feedback about a match recommendation.
This data is used to retrain the ML model.

**One feedback per match** — returns 409 if feedback already exists.
Submitting feedback also sets `action_taken=true` on the match.

**Feedback types:**
- `relevant` — positive signal, the match was a good recommendation
- `not_relevant` — negative signal, the match was a poor fit
- `already_connected` — user already knows this person/project
- `not_interested` — user is not interested right now

get.description:
Returns a summary of the current matches and feedback tables.
Use this before deciding whether to trigger a new generation run.

post.description:
Generates synthetic user profiles, projects, and labelled match pairs
using the same scoring weights as the production recommendation model.

All parameters are optional — omitted values use the same defaults
as the `MLMatchDatasetSeeder`.

Set `fresh: true` to wipe existing match data first.
**Use with caution in production** — this deletes real user feedback.

get.description:
Returns flattened training rows with all feature columns and labels.

**JSON** — returned in the response body.
**CSV** — streamed as a file download (same format as `ml:export-matches` CLI).

`feedback_type` / `label_relevant` are populated from end-user
feedback submitted via `POST /matches/{id}/feedback`.

parameters.name: with_feedback_only
parameters.description: Only return rows with user feedback — reduces noise for classification training

schema.description: File download — same column layout as JSON data array

post.description:
Accepts ML-scored match pairs and writes them to the `matches` table.
End users then see the results at `GET /matches`.

- Existing non-expired records for the same user+target are **updated**
  (score, reasons, expiry).
- New pairs are **created**.

Max 1,000 records per call — batch larger payloads across multiple requests.

422.description: Validation error (invalid UUIDs, wrong type/target combination)

UserRole.description:
- `guest`          — ephemeral session (issued by /auth/guest)
- `regular_user`   — standard registered account
- `moderator`      — content moderator
- `administrator`  — full platform access

AccountStatus.description:
- `pending`   — registered, email not yet verified; token issued but write routes blocked
- `active`    — email verified; full access
- `suspended` — temporarily blocked by admin
- `banned`    — permanently blocked
- `deleted`   — soft-deleted

MatchedUser.description: Populated only when match_type is collaborator

MatchedProject.description: Populated only when match_type is project

match_reasons.description:
Feature breakdown from the ML model.
Collaborator keys: skill_overlap, complementarity, location_match, both_identity_verified
Project keys: skill_coverage, team_openness, project_accepting, user_identity_verified

status_label.description: Human-readable label for the current status

liveness_check_passed.description: Set by ML processing after submission

face_match_score.description: 0.0–1.0 face match confidence from liveness SDK

rejection_reason.description: Only populated when verification_status is rejected

TrainingRow.description:
A single flattened training sample.

Feature columns by match_type:
- **collaborator**: skill_overlap, complementarity, overlapping_skills_count,
  skills_count_a, skills_count_b, both_identity_verified,
  user_a_verified, user_b_verified, location_match
- **project**: skill_coverage, covered_skills_count, required_skills_count,
  user_skills_count, team_openness, project_accepting, user_identity_verified

Label columns (ML targets):
- `compatibility_score` — regression target (0.0–1.0)
- `label_relevant` — binary classification target (1 = user said "relevant")
- `label_not_relevant` — binary classification target

feedback_type.description: Empty string if no feedback yet

match_reasons.description: Feature breakdown displayed to end users to explain the match

call_type.description: Derived automatically from the context ID provided at initiation. `conversation` when linked to a conversation; `project` when linked to a project. Never sent by the client.

room_name.description: Unique Jitsi room identifier (`cofound-` + 16 random chars)

room_url.description:
Bare Jitsi Meet URL (no token). **Only returned to confirmed participants.** Non-participants receive `null`.
**Do not open this URL directly** — it will be rejected by the Jitsi server. Always append `?jwt={join_token}` obtained from `POST /calls` (initiator) or `POST /calls/{id}/join` (others).

join_token.description:
Short-lived Jitsi JWT (HS256) scoped to this room and user. **Present only on `POST /calls` (201) and `POST /calls/{id}/join` (200) responses.** Never returned by GET endpoints.
Build the final Jitsi URL as: `{room_url}?jwt={join_token}`
Expires after 4 hours. Call `/join` again to obtain a fresh token (e.g. after a page refresh).
